daily.readme: # Modern Web Guidance (Source) This repo is the source repository for [GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance) and includes the code and documentation for authoring, calibrating, and evaluating its contents. [**Modern Web Guidance**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into your coding agents. It helps to steer your coding agents away from legacy patterns, and instead toward solutions that harness the power and capabilities of the modern web platform. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) and [GOVERNANCE.md](./GOVERNANCE.md) for how we work on the project and orientation of the codebase. --- *Stewarded by the Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN teams, alongside the web development community.* [Documentation](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) · [Eval Dashboard](https://googlechrome.github.io/modern-web-guidance-src/) · [Source Code](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src) · [Report an Issue](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/issues) ## Quickstart ```shell npx modern-web-guidance@latest install ``` This command runs an interactive wizard to install Modern Web Guidance. See [Alternative Installation Methods](#-alternative-installation-methods) below. #### Try it out (without installing) ```shell # Search for relevant guides npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate a dialog modal backdrop" # Retrieve a guide by ID npx modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "animate-to-from-top-layer" # Scan a codebase for legacy patterns to modernize

daily.desc: OpenAI's Codex Security CLI and TypeScript SDK for finding, validating, and fixing security vulnerabilities. npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openai/codex-security
daily.readme:
# Codex Security

Codex Security helps you find, investigate, and fix vulnerabilities in your code.
Use its security workflows in Codex, or automate them with the
`@openai/codex-security` CLI and TypeScript SDK.

- **In Codex:** [choose a security workflow](docs/agent-workflows.md).
- **In a terminal:** [install the CLI and scan your repository](#quick-start).
- **In automation:** use the [TypeScript SDK](#typescript-sdk) or
  [GitHub Action](#github-actions).

## Features

- Scan repositories, selected paths, or Git changes. Deep scans repeat Standard scans and return their deduplicated findings.
- Validate candidate findings, generate patches, and verify existing fixes.
- Draft `SECURITY.md` policies and save threat models for later review.
- Browse saved scans and findings, identify duplicates, assess severity against
  your own rubric, and suggest owners from source and Git history.
- Preview third-party scanner findings, save them locally, or publish supported reports to Codex Security Cloud. [Scanner import guides](docs/scanner-imports/README.md).
- Track findings in Linear, Jira, or GitHub, publish completed scans, or export SARIF, JSON, and CSV. [Integration workflows](docs/plugin-connectors.md).
- Automate scans across repositories or project components, including in CI and
  containers.

## Use in Codex

Open your repository in a Codex session with the Codex Security plugin enabled,
then ask:

> Run a Codex Security scan on this repository, focusing on authentication and
> authorization. Return the saved report, source evidence, and coverage limits.

A completed scan saves a report and findings. Read the report for source
evidence and exclusions, then request a patch or ask Codex to verify an
existing fix. See the [agent workflow guide](docs/agent-workflows.md) for setup,
task selection, and recovery.

## Quick start

Requires Node.js 22.13.0+ within 22.x, or Node.js 24.x or 26.x, and Python 3.10+.
Python 3.10 also requires `tomli`.

daily.readme:
# HermesEnabler 2

[English](README.md) · [한국어](README.ko.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md) · [Español](README.es.md) · [Français](README.fr.md) · [Deutsch](README.de.md) · [Português](README.pt.md)

![](image.png)

> Supported only on watchOS 27.0 through 27.3 beta 1.

## Installation

### macOS

On macOS you can install the prebuilt IPA with Sideloadly or build the app directly with Xcode. Either way, the iPhone must be paired with the target Apple Watch, and the Watch must run a supported watchOS version.

#### Install the IPA

> **Known issue with Sideloadly 0.72:** [Issue #43](https://github.com/pookjw/HermesEnabler/issues/43) reports that this version may remove the embedded Watch app while signing. If the iPhone app installs but HermesEnabler2 is missing from the Watch, use Xcode instead. This report is specific to version 0.72; compatibility with other versions has not been confirmed.

1. Download the IPA from [Releases](https://github.com/pookjw/HermesEnabler/releases).
2. Install [Sideloadly](https://sideloadly.io) on your Mac, connect your iPhone with a cable, and select it in Sideloadly.
3. Drag the IPA into Sideloadly and enter your Apple ID. Turn off **Use automatic bundle ID**, set a fixed Bundle Identifier, and start signing.
4. On the iPhone, open **Settings → General → VPN & Device Management** and trust your developer certificate.
5. On the iPhone, open **Settings → Privacy & Security → Developer Mode**, turn it on, restart, and confirm.
6. On the iPhone, open the **Watch** app, go to **My Watch → Apps**, and install **HermesEnabler2** on the Watch.
7. On the Apple Watch, open **Settings → Privacy & Security → Developer Mode**, turn it on, restart, and confirm. If the option is not shown, install the Watch app first and check again.
8. Open **HermesEnabler2** on your Apple Watch and follow the steps in the app.

#### Build with Xcode

1. Open [HermesEnabler2.xcodeproj](HermesEnabler2.xcodeproj) in Xcode.

daily.desc: LLM Inference Engine for Metal, CUDA and Vulkan.
daily.readme:
# TensorFold

TensorFold serves language models from a Zig binary on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs.
The engine reads checkpoints, tokenizes requests and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly.
Serving needs no Python or MLX installation.

Building with a coding agent? Have it load the [contributor skill](docs/recipes/SKILL.md) before it writes any code.

## Contributing with agents

Please use [Agent Traffic Control](https://github.com/ashhart/ATC) before editing TensorFold so contributors and agents can avoid duplicate work and conflicting changes.
Check the [live agent radar](https://tensorfold.dev/atc) before choosing an issue and follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [ATC contributor instructions](docs/atc/SKILL.md).

Install or upgrade ATC to 0.9.4 or later, then run from an updated TensorFold clone:

```sh
npm install -g github:ashhart/ATC
atc check ISSUE --json
atc claim ISSUE --json
```

Replace `ISSUE` with the issue number and claim only after a complete check says the work is free.
TensorFold enables automatic public check-ins: a successful new claim starts an anonymous session on the radar and returns its `session` number.
Keep that number instead of starting a duplicate session.
For work already yours, start a session with `atc start ISSUE --json`.
Add `--github-name` to `claim` or `start` only if you want your verified GitHub name shown; `--local` keeps a new session on your machine.
The board shows the issue, activity state and last check-in; GitHub still associates the verification comment with its author.
Check that `publication` is `public`; `unavailable` means the public update failed even if the local claim or session succeeded.

Pulse only while the agent is working, before its five-minute check-in expires:

```sh
atc pulse ISSUE SESSION working --json
atc who path/to/file --json
atc overlap --json
atc land ISSUE SESSION --json
atc release ISSUE --json
```

# Node.js

Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime environment.

For information on using Node.js, see the [Node.js website][].

The Node.js project uses an [open governance model](./GOVERNANCE.md). The
[OpenJS Foundation][] provides support for the project.

Contributors are expected to act in a collaborative manner to move
the project forward. We encourage the constructive exchange of contrary
opinions and compromise. The [TSC](./GOVERNANCE.md#technical-steering-committee)
reserves the right to limit or block contributors who repeatedly act in ways
that discourage, exhaust, or otherwise negatively affect other participants.

**This project has a [Code of Conduct][].**

## Table of contents

* [Support](#support)
* [Release types](#release-types)
  * [Download](#download)
    * [Current and LTS releases](#current-and-lts-releases)
    * [Nightly releases](#nightly-releases)
    * [API documentation](#api-documentation)
  * [Verifying binaries](#verifying-binaries)
* [Building Node.js](#building-nodejs)
* [Security](#security)
* [Contributing to Node.js](#contributing-to-nodejs)
* [Current project team members](#current-project-team-members)
  * [TSC (Technical Steering Committee)](#tsc-technical-steering-committee)
  * [Collaborators](#collaborators)
  * [Triagers](#triagers)
  * [Release keys](#release-keys)
* [License](#license)

## Support

Looking for help? Check out the
[instructions for getting support](.github/SUPPORT.md).

## Release types

Node.js follows [semantic versioning](https://semver.org).

* **Alpha**: Under active development where semver-major changes are allowed.
  Each October, a new release line (for example, Node.js 27) branches off `main`
  and receives Alpha releases (for example, `27.0.0-alpha.0.0.0`) for 6 months,
  then are promoted to Current (see below) each April. Alpha releases are signed,
  tagged, and tested through [CITGM](https://github.com/nodejs/citgm), but their
  API and ABI may change between releases.
